_comment: The only place that knows anything model-specific. Read by run_eval.sh (via a
python3 one-liner) and by the drivers directly, so bash and python cannot drift
apart -- which they would if the serve flags lived in a case statement here and a
dict there.
serve_flags is the difference between 'serves' and 'does not serve'. Muse-Glimmer
emits channel-scoped messages and needs BOTH its parsers or every turn mis-parses;
Qwen3.5 needs its reasoning parser or the chain of thought lands in `content` and
gets scored as the answer. Neither is optional and neither is discoverable from the
config, so both are written down.
quantize.ignore / quantize.expect drive bin/quantize_rtn.py: what to leave in bf16,
and a regex the resolved target set must match exactly. expect is checked against
the result rather than used to build it, so a change in either the model layout or
llm-compressor's pattern expansion is caught before any GPU time is spent.
kv_buffer_device is cuda on EVERY model. It registers the KV blocks with NIXL
directly in VRAM instead of staging them through host memory.
It used to be per model, and that was a mistake left standing too long. cuda was set
only where it was FORCED -- the hybrid SSM models, whose host staging buffers are
built for attention layers only, so a Mamba layer's descriptors point into VRAM while
a cpu-staged agent registers as DRAM and the handshake fails with NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND.
The attention-only models kept cpu because that is what muse-glimmer's published
numbers were measured with, which is a reason to record a number, not a reason to
serve every later model that way.
What that cost: gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, an MoE, disaggregated through host staging and
produced corrupted output on OCRBench -- 138 truncations against 22 single-engine on
bf16-pd, 182 against 35 on nvfp4pd, decode-side `invalid prefix detokenization`
errors, and token-level garbage in the outputs. The dense gemma-4-31b-it, same
sliding_window and same cpu setting, shows none of it. Whether cuda fixes the MoE
case is being measured rather than assumed.
report.baseline / report.arms are what compare_arms.py uses when not told
otherwise. The baseline must be an arm with REPEATS: a single-pass arm has no
spread to build an interval from, so every comparison against it comes out
single-engine bf16 is the baseline on every model, so the reference is the same serving
models bf16-pd is a one-pass sanity check that disaggregation serves this
topology everywhere and bf16-pd is a reported arm measuring what disaggregation itself costs.
as an arm whose interval will honestly read as unresolved.
nvfp4-gptq is the third-party GPTQ W4A4 checkpoint from daslab-testing, listed as
an arm so it is scored and tested like any other. It is only an ALGORITHM
comparison against `nvfp4` because both quantize the same module set -- verified
per model, and the reason Qwen's ignore list now excludes the DeltaNet gates.
The baseline is single-engine bf16 on EVERY model. It is the one reference that
exists with 4 passes everywhere, so the three models are compared against the same
kind of thing by construction rather than by argument. bf16-pd was the baseline on
muse-glimmer while it was the only model with 4 passes of it; that made muse's
quantized arms measured against a disaggregated reference while the others were
measured against a single-engine one, an inconsistency resting on the null result
that disaggregation is accuracy-neutral rather than on the design. bf16-pd is now
an arm on all three, where its own comparison against bf16 is the thing that
reports that null instead of assuming it.
nemotron-3-omni-30b has no GPTQ arms: daslab-testing has published no checkpoint
for it, so nvfp4-gptq and lut3-nvfp4-gptq simply do not exist here. Its arms are
the ones this repo produces itself.
lut3-nvfp4-gptq is the phase-disaggregated pair built from the two GPTQ
checkpoints: NVFP4 (W4A4) on prefill, LUT3 on decode. Both are PSEUDO-QUANTIZED
for LUT3 -- the lloyd43 checkpoints are full bf16 (55 GB, same size as the base)
whose values already lie on the 3-bit Lloyd grid -- so they are served by vanilla
vLLM with no --quantization flag and no packing plugin. The kernels in
qad/kernels/lloyd43 are NOT involved and must not be, since re-packing would
change what is being measured.

notes: Thinking is ON by default and the vendor's thinking-mode settings are exactly
what generation_config.json carries (temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20),
so --generation-config auto gives the recommended configuration with no extra
flags. The non-thinking preset differs (0.7 / 0.80 / 20 / presence_penalty 1.5)
and is NOT what is measured here.
Hybrid architecture: 48 Gated-DeltaNet linear-attention layers interleaved with
16 gated-attention layers, plus MTP weights. Disaggregated serving DOES work --
NixlConnector transfers the recurrent SSM state alongside KV -- but it needs two
things this model would not otherwise get: VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS (set in
evals/serving/run_nixl_server.sh) and kv_buffer_device=cuda, because host staging
buffers are built for attention layers only.
a --disagg arm on this model; MMMU single-engine does not depend on it.
No published MMMU or MMMU-Pro score. GPQA-Diamond is reported as 89.2.
DO NOT QUANTIZE linear_attn.in_proj_a / in_proj_b. They are the Gated DeltaNet
gating projections that set the recurrent state decay: 96 modules, 11.8M of 12.2G
quantized weight elements (0.097%), so quantizing them saves nothing measurable
while putting 4-bit noise directly on the state-decay path. The reference NVFP4
checkpoints from daslab-testing leave them in bf16, and Qwen is also the model
that lost the most to W4A4 (-5.09 against Gemma's -2.02), so the earlier recipe
was plausibly paying for it. 400 quantized linears, not 496.
Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration, dense (enable_moe_block=false), 60 decoder
layers, vision tower present and audio_config null despite the audio token ids.
Ordinary attention throughout, so the SSM machinery Qwen needs does not apply
and kv_buffer_device can stay cpu.
TIED EMBEDDINGS: there is no lm_head tensor in the checkpoint at all. It stays
in the ignore list regardless, because compressed-tensors names the module and
not the tensor -- dropping it would be relying on the absence of a weight to
protect the output projection.
attention_k_eq_v: v_proj exists in only 50 of the 60 layers -- ten layers share
K and V. So per_layer is null and the expected count is 410, not 60*7=420. A
uniform-layer assumption would fail the count check on a correct model.
The vision tower nests its linears one level deeper as `q_proj.linear.weight`,
which the `.*vision_tower.*` pattern still covers. `embed_vision` is the
projection into the text stream and is ignored for the same reason the
projector is on every other model here.
nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-BF16, 62 GiB. Hybrid Nemotron-H:
52 layers on the pattern MEMEM*EMEMEM*... -- 23 Mamba2 (M), 23 MoE (E, 128
routed experts top-6 plus one shared expert), 6 attention (*). Vision tower is
RADIO, and there is a sound encoder plus projector this benchmark never exercises.
vLLM registers NemotronH_Nano_Omni_Reasoning_V3 natively, so the architecture is
not coming from the repo's remote code even though --trust-remote-code is passed;
the flag is there because the config's auto_map still points at configuration.py.
NO TOOL PARSER. The model card asks for --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder, and this
container's vLLM has no such parser -- vllm/tool_parsers ships qwen3_engine, not
qwen3_coder. Nothing here sends tools, so tool calling is not configured rather
than configured wrongly. Add it before running anything that does use tools.
kv_buffer_device is cuda for the same reason as Qwen3.8: 23 of the 52 layers are
Mamba2, host staging buffers are built for attention layers only, and a cpu-staged
agent fails registration with NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND. Disaggregated arms also need
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS, which evals/serving/run_nixl_server.sh already sets.
QUANTIZE TARGETS: ALL MLP AND ATTENTION, NOT MAMBA AND NOT THE ROUTER. 5958
linears -- 5888 routed-expert up/down, 46 shared-expert up/down, 24 attention
q/k/v/o. That is 90.8% of the 33.02B parameters and 39.4% of the 5.02B active per
token. Adding the mamba in/out projections would reach 93.5% of total for 2.0 GiB
more on a 61.5 GiB checkpoint -- 3% -- while putting 4-bit on the state-decay path,
which is not a trade worth making. The router is 0.02% of weights and 4-bit noise
there changes WHICH experts run rather than perturbing an output.
NVIDIA's own NVFP4 build is MIXED_PRECISION and differs: FP4 on the routed experts
only, FP8 on mamba in/out, shared experts and o_proj, BF16 on q/k/v. Their FP8 tier
is a coverage trick -- it reaches ~55% of ACTIVE parameters, which is what decode
bandwidth actually reads, without spending 4 bits on mamba. A single-precision
recipe is used here so nvfp4 / nvfp4a16 / nvfp4pd stay a clean A4-vs-A16 contrast
on one module set, the way they are on the other three models.
The router (mixer.gate, 23 modules) is ignored. It picks 6 of 128 experts from a
2688-wide logit, it is 0.005% of the weights, and 4-bit noise on it changes WHICH
experts run rather than perturbing an output. conv1d is Conv1d and llm-compressor
targets Linear, so it needs no entry.
THINKING HAS NO FORCED END WITHOUT `thinking_token_budget`. It is a request-body
field, not a generation_config one, so no server-side setting supplies it and the
no-client-side-sampling rule cannot cover it. Without it 989 of 6920 MMMU items
(14%) and 971 of 7400 OCRBench items ran to the token cap and returned EMPTY
content -- against 2 and 7 for Gemma -- and bf16 read 52.90 where the other three
models sit at 66-75. Quantized arms are hit far harder: every one of 8 smoke items
truncated, on NVIDIA's own A4 module set as much as on ours, because a slightly
degraded model thinks longer and falls into the runaway regime more often. No
conclusion about W4A4 on this model is available from a run without this set.
max_tokens is the vendor's 20480 rather than the 32768 the other models use, since
thinking stops at 16384 + 1024 grace and the rest is the answer. generation_config
supplies temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 and no top_k.
NO W4A4 ARM. Every NVFP4 variant built for this model is degenerate: it never stops
generating and returns empty content on every item. Measured with the vendor's
thinking budget enforced, 16/16 smoke items empty at the token cap, on THREE
different module sets -- all MLP+attention (5958 linears), that minus mamba, and
NVIDIA's own FP4 set of routed experts only (5888). The abandoned runs are on disk
as evidence: 128/128 empty on mmmu/nvfp4 and mmmu/nvfp4pd.
The weights are not the problem. NVFP4A16 quantizes the SAME modules to 4 bits and
is healthy (0/16 truncated, p50 2832 tokens), so it is the 4-bit ACTIVATIONS, and it
does not depend on where they are applied. Since NVIDIA ships a working NVFP4 build
on a module set that fails here, the suspect is this repo's calibration rather than
the format -- unproven, and deliberately not chased.
nvfp4 and nvfp4pd are therefore OUT of report.arms: leaving them in would print
'still generating' forever for runs that were stopped on purpose. The finding is
that W4A4 is not measurable on this model with this pipeline, not that it scored 0.
nvfp4-nv IS NVIDIA'S OWN CHECKPOINT, not this repo's RTN output, and is NOT the same
format as `nvfp4` on the other models. Theirs is MIXED_PRECISION: NVFP4 W4A4 on the
5888 routed-expert projections, FP8 W8A8 on mamba in/out, the shared experts and
attention o_proj, BF16 on q/k/v, and an FP8 KV cache. This repo's `nvfp4` means W4A4
on every language-model linear. Do not read nvfp4-nv against another model's nvfp4
column as a like-for-like comparison -- the cross-model contrasts use `nvfp4`, and
nemotron correctly reports no data there.
It also WORKS, where every checkpoint this repo's pipeline produced was degenerate on
all three module sets tried. That points at the calibration here rather than at the
format or the architecture, and is left as an observation rather than chased.
nvfp4-nv-pd is that checkpoint disaggregated with ACTIVATION QUANTIZATION DISABLED ON
DECODE and no other change: the 5888 routed-expert entries in quantized_layers are
relabelled NVFP4 -> W4A16_NVFP4, which vLLM supports natively with identical packing
and group size. Weights are byte-identical -- the decode directory symlinks the same
safetensors and differs only in config.json.
Two things it deliberately does not change. The 98 FP8 layers stay W8A8: vLLM offers
FP8 / FP8_PER_CHANNEL_PER_TOKEN / FP8_PB_WO and none is a per-tensor weight-only
match for this checkpoint's scales, so disabling their activation quantization would
need re-quantization. And kv_cache_scheme stays FP8 on both engines, because it is
the KV cache dtype rather than an activation and a disaggregated pair must agree on
it or the transferred cache is uninterpretable.
config_groups/input_activations is NOT the control. vLLM's MIXED_PRECISION path never
reads that field -- editing it changed nothing and the first attempt at this arm was
a no-op that still served. quantized_layers is what it reads. Confirm the relabel took
effect by the MoE backend in the server log: FLASHINFER_TRTLLM for W4A4, MARLIN for
weight-only.
google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it, 51.6 GB. SAME ARCHITECTURE CLASS as gemma-4-31b-it --
Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration, model_type gemma4, gemma4_vision tower -- but with
enable_moe_block true: 128 experts, top-8, moe_intermediate_size 704. 30 layers,
25 sliding_attention (window 1024) plus 5 full_attention. So the serve flags are the
31B's and no --trust-remote-code is needed; vLLM registers the architecture natively.
generation_config is identical to the 31B's (temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 /
top_k 64), so --generation-config auto gives the vendor's settings and the
launcher's sampling guard covers it. No thinking_token_budget equivalent: unlike
Nemotron, reasoning ends on a stop token, so request_extra_body is not needed.
THE EXPERTS ARE FUSED 3-D TENSORS, not per-expert modules: 1013 tensors in the
checkpoint where 30 layers x 128 experts x 3 projections would be ~11,500. They
appear as mlp.gate_proj / up_proj / down_proj once per layer. Whether
llm-compressor's targets=Linear reaches them is a question the dry run answers --
a fused expert bank is typically an nn.Parameter inside a custom module rather than
an nn.Linear, in which case only the 120 attention projections resolve and the arm
would quantize ~none of the model. Do not launch a quantize job before checking the
resolved count.
The router is model.language_model.layers.N.router.proj and is ignored, as on
nemotron: 4-bit noise on it changes WHICH experts run rather than perturbing an
output, for a negligible share of the weights.
MoE CONCURRENCY, the lesson from nemotron: top-8 of 128 means (1 - 8/128)^B of
experts go untouched at batch B, so batch 32 reads ~87% of the expert weights for
32 tokens and the A4B sparsity buys almost nothing. Run this model with
--workers 512 --max-num-seqs 512 like nemotron, not the 32 default.
2.4T total / 95B active, 512 experts top-10, 92 layers of which 69 are
Gated-DeltaNet linear attention and 23 full attention. TEXT ONLY
(Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM, model_type qwen3_5_moe_text): there is no vision tower and
no preprocessor in the repo, so MMMU-Pro cannot be run on it at all. MMLU-Pro is
the only benchmark here that applies.
nnodes/tensor_parallel_size are sized for the LARGEST arm, fp8 at 2.50 TB: 16 GPUs
over 4 trays is 4.08 TB at 0.90 utilisation. TP must divide the 64 attention heads,
so 16 is the next legal size above 8 -- and 8 GPUs is 2.04 TB, which does not hold
fp8 at all. The 4-bit arms are ~1.25 TB and fit TP=8 on 2 nodes; pass --nnodes 2
--tp 8 for those. One value per model cannot express a per-arm topology, and the
flag is the honest way to say it rather than a schema that pretends otherwise.
The vendor recipe also passes --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser
qwen3_coder. Omitted: no benchmark here calls tools, and an unused tool parser is
one more thing that can mis-parse a turn. --reasoning-parser qwen3 is NOT optional,
for the same reason it is not on qwen3.8-27b: without it the chain of thought lands
in `content` and gets scored as the answer.
BASELINE IS fp8, NOT bf16. bf16 is 4.89 TB -- TP=32 over 8 nodes for the reference
arm alone, four times over for the repeats. Every delta reported for this model is
therefore the cost of 4-bit RELATIVE TO FP8, which is not the same quantity as the
bf16-baselined numbers on the other models in this repo. Do not put them in one
column without saying so.
Hybrid, so the same two requirements as qwen3.8-27b: VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS
and kv_buffer_device=cuda. 69 of 92 layers are linear attention here against 48 of
64 there, so it matters more, not less.
THE EXPERTS ARE FUSED: mlp.experts.gate_up_proj and mlp.experts.down_proj are single
stacked tensors covering all 512 experts, not 512 separate modules. That is the one
structural difference from every model already quantized here, and quantize.expect
below is written against it rather than against per-expert names.

shared_expert_gate stays bf16, like the routers on the other MoE models here: it selects whether the shared expert contributes, so 4-bit noise on it moves a routing decision rather than a value, and it is 92 vectors.
1.56 TB of MXFP4 weights as released: compressed-tensors mxfp4-pack-quantized,
per-expert 2D weight_packed/weight_scale, 247,296 quantized modules over 93 layers
(24 full attention, 69 linear) and 896 experts. Multimodal, so unlike
qwen3.8-2.4t this one CAN run MMMU-Pro.
mxfp4a16 IS the released checkpoint -- input_activations is null in its own config,
so what ships is weight-only. The mxfp4 arm is the same weight FILES by symlink with
input_activations added; MXFP4 activations are dynamic (observer=None), so there is
no calibration, no extra tensor and no repack. Kimi-K3-a4 is 106 KB on disk.
That is the difference from gpt-oss-120b, which ships quant_method=mxfp4 with fused
3D *_blocks/*_scales and cannot express W4A4 at all in its native vLLM path -- it
needs bin/repack_mxfp4.py first. Same format name, different checkpoints.
96 attention heads AND 96 KV heads (MHA, not GQA) across the 24 full-attention
layers, so KV per token is large. tensor_parallel_size is 8 over 2 nodes for the
1.56 TB of weights; if the KV pool comes up short, the fix is more nodes rather
than fewer sequences.
sampling_guard=false: generation_config.json is {max_length, eos_token_id} with no
temperature/top_p/top_k, so vLLM logs no override and the guard would abort a healthy
server after 60s. Measured with vLLM's own sampling defaults.
The mxfp4 variant copies the remote-code .py files rather than symlinking them: with
symlinks, transformers' dynamic module loader fails on the relative import inside
media_utils with ModuleNotFoundError on transformers_modules.<dir>.<hash>. Only the
1.5 TB of safetensors is symlinked.
mxfp4pd is the repo's mixed arm in MXFP4 form: W4A4 prefill feeding W4A16 decode, the
same direction as nvfp4pd everywhere else. Both engines load the SAME weight files --
Kimi-K3-a4 and Kimi-K3 differ only in input_activations -- so the pair isolates where
activation quantization is applied, with nothing else varying. NixlConnector's compat
hash covers the model path string, so NIXL_ENFORCE_COMPAT=0 opens automatically.
REASONING_EFFORT high, NOT max. Kimi's renderer accepts exactly four values --
vllm/renderers/kimi_k3.py matches ['high','low','max','none'] and there is no
'medium', so high IS the middle setting for this model. Moonshot's published numbers
use max; these do not, and are therefore not comparable to the model card.
top_p 0.95 is a DELIBERATE EXCEPTION to the no-client-side-sampling rule. Every other
model here lets --generation-config auto apply the vendor's values, but Kimi's
generation_config.json is {max_length, eos_token_id} with no sampling at all -- which
is why sampling_guard is false -- so the server has nothing to apply and would fall
back to vLLM's top_p 1.0. The vendor asks for 0.95 on non-agentic tasks. temperature
is NOT sent: vLLM's default is already the vendor's 1.0.
The -nothink arms were measured before any of this, with reasoning_parser='' and no
effort field. Kimi always thinks, so the channel markers leaked into content on
12025/12032 rows and the think channel opened and closed empty. Those runs are kept
under the -nothink suffix rather than deleted: they are the thinking-off baseline,
and the delta against the thinking arms is worth having.
BF16 SOURCE, so this model gets NVFP4 like every other model here -- MXFP4 is only
for checkpoints that ship it natively (kimi-k3). 247 GB over 50 shards, ungated.
88 backbone layers: 40 mamba, 40 MoE, 8 attention. 512 experts top-22, stored
PER-EXPERT 2D (experts.N.up_proj / down_proj), so linearize_moe is not needed --
unlike gemma-4-26b-a4b-it, whose experts arrive fused.
NO BIASES on anything quantized: attention_bias, mlp_bias and mamba_proj_bias are
all false and the checkpoint has zero expert or attention bias tensors. That is what
makes it servable through compressed-tensors at all; gpt-oss-120b was dropped
precisely because its experts carry biases that vLLM's compressed-tensors MoE never
registers, so no repack of it could load.
What stays bf16, following nemotron-3-omni-30b: the router (mixer.gate), the mamba
in_proj/out_proj, the MTP tower, and lm_head. The mamba projections are the
recurrent path, and 4-bit noise there is the same hazard as Qwen's DeltaNet gates.
fc1/fc2_latent_proj are left bf16 too -- 40 modules against 20,480 experts, so they
cost nothing to skip and are not what 'experts and attention' means.
NemotronHForCausalLM with NO remote code -- no auto_map, no .py files -- so it needs
neither --trust-remote-code nor mamba-ssm. That is what makes it usable where the
Super 120B is not: the Super's shipped modeling file hard-raises
'mamba-ssm is required by the Mamba model but cannot be imported', and mamba-ssm is
sdist-only with no aarch64 wheels.
nemotron_v3, matching the vendor's own serve line. The earlier deepseek_r1 setting
rested on the claim that nemotron_v3 is an engine-token parser with no <think>
markers. That is false. vllm/parser/nemotron_v3.py says outright: "The Nemotron 3
Super model uses the same tool call and reasoning format as Qwen3 (<think>/</think>
+ <tool_call> XML)", and NemotronV3Parser subclasses Qwen3Parser reusing qwen3_config.
It is token-id based rather than string based, but the tokens ARE <think>/</think>,
so it keys on exactly what this chat template emits.
deepseek_r1 did work -- it is not a broken setting, and bf16/nvfp4a16-nv measured
under it are internally consistent. It fails only on truncated generations: the
template pre-opens <think> at line 186, so the model emits only the CLOSING tag, and
when the token cap arrives first there is no </think>, deepseek_r1 puts the entire
output in reasoning and returns EMPTY content. That is 38 rows of the bf16 run,
exactly matching its 38 finish_reason=length rows. NVIDIA wrote
super_v3_reasoning_parser.py, a DeepSeekR1ReasoningParser subclass, to patch this
same failure -- which is evidence the family's format is <think>-based, but not
evidence that deepseek_r1 is the parser to use unpatched.
force_nonempty_content is what actually fixes those rows. NemotronV3Parser swaps
reasoning into content when content comes back empty, but ONLY when
chat_template_kwargs carries enable_thinking=False or force_nonempty_content=True.
Neither is sent by default, so the parser alone would leave the 38 rows empty. It is
a chat_template_kwargs key this template never reads, so it is inert in the jinja and
read only by the parser, and the swap is gated on content being empty -- untruncated
rows are untouched.
The sampling guard STAYS ON here: generation_config.json carries temperature 1.0 and
top_p 0.95, so vLLM does log the override and there is something real to assert --
unlike kimi-k3 and the dropped gpt-oss-120b, whose configs carry no sampling at all.
nvfp4-nv is NVIDIA's released checkpoint and is WEIGHT-ONLY despite the name: its
quantization_config has two groups -- group_1 is 5,935 NVFP4 modules with
input_activations null, and group_0 is 46 mamba in_proj/out_proj already at FP8 W8A8.
So it is a W4A16 arm plus a little FP8, not W4A4.
The planned nvfp4 arm calibrates activation scales ON TOP of those 4-bit weights
rather than requantizing from bf16: NVFP4 activations are not dynamic (observer
static_minmax), and vLLM's modelopt path takes static input_scale only -- it says
outright that dynamic support 'might be added'. So a config edit cannot work here the
way it does for kimi-k3's MXFP4.
The released checkpoint is tagged nvfp4a16-nv, NOT nvfp4-nv. It is weight-only, and
on nemotron-3-omni-30b the tag nvfp4-nv already means NVIDIA's W4A4 checkpoint -- one
tag meaning W4A4 on one model and W4A16 on another is how a cross-model table ends up
comparing unlike arms. The -nv suffix marks the vendor's checkpoint; the a16 says what
it actually is.
NemotronHForCausalLM, 550B total / 55B active. 512 routed experts top-22 plus one
shared expert, hidden 8192, moe_latent_size 2048, 64 attention heads / 2 KV heads,
mamba_num_heads 256. Same nemotron_h family as the Super and the 3.5 Lightning.
nnodes 2 / tp 8 follows the vendor's own --tensor-parallel-size 8. 1.1 TB of bf16
weights against 8 x 288 GB at 0.90 utilisation is 2.07 TB, leaving ~0.9 TB for KV.
TP must divide the 64 attention heads, which 8 does.
server_pythonpath is the muse-mambadeps overlay for the same reason as the Super:
the nemotron_h remote code hard-raises if mamba_ssm cannot be imported, and the
container ships neither mamba-ssm nor causal-conv1d (sdist-only, no aarch64 wheels,
so both were built from source).
reasoning parser nemotron_v3 and force_nonempty_content for the same reasons as
nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b -- see that entry. The sampling guard STAYS ON: this
generation_config.json carries temperature 1.0 and top_p 0.95, so there is a real
override for the guard to assert.
eos_token_id is a LIST, [2, 11], unlike every other model here. Nothing in the
harness depends on that, but it is the sort of thing that breaks a stop condition.
TWO QUANTIZATION STACKS, deliberately. The -nv arms are NVIDIA's released ModelOpt
MIXED_PRECISION checkpoint (192 FP8 + 49,152 NVFP4, lm_head NOT quantized at all);
the un-suffixed arms are this repo's compressed-tensors RTN from bf16 (49,296
linears). Same model, same benchmark, two independent paths -- which is the point,
since nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b loses 10 points at W4A4 on the ModelOpt path while
nemotron-3-super-120b loses 0.2 on compressed-tensors, and Ultra is the case that
separates 'the ModelOpt path is broken' from 'that checkpoint is broken'.
nvfp4a16-nv is the SAME WEIGHTS as nvfp4-nv with all 49,152 modules relabelled
NVFP4 -> W4A16_NVFP4 and the shards symlinked, so the pair differs only in whether
activations are quantized. Its input_scale tensors are left in place: on the ModelOpt
path ModelOptNvFp4W4A16LinearMethod registers input_scale and ignores it. That is NOT
true of compressed-tensors, where a leftover input_global_scale is a hard load error
